title: SRD coverage: constructs, animated objects and awakened plants
summary: Independently authored GURPS builds for the 6 identities issue #42 enumerates. These are the first records in the coverage program with no metabolism, which is exactly the case issue #17 flagged: the rating path reads FP and DR, and a thing that has neither is easy to under-rate. Every construct here therefore states FP explicitly rather than leaving it to fall out of HT, and every one buys its Injury Tolerance from the published parts — Homogenous for an object that is the same all the way through, Unliving for a golem that is at least shaped like a body. Animated objects are built as blind: they have no eyes at all, and the awareness that replaces sight is bought as Vibration Sense, which is a much better description of what a walking suit of armor actually does. Size Modifier is read off the published table keyed to longest dimension; ST comes from Basic Lift and from what the thing demonstrably shifts.

monsters.name: Animated Armor
monsters.lair: The hall it was set to watch, standing where a suit of armor would be expected to stand.

attacks.name: Gauntlet
attacks.notes: A steel fist swung with the whole weight of the harness behind it.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: It walks into a target and keeps walking.

monsters.description: An empty suit of plate that turns its helm toward a sound and then comes down the hall. There is nothing inside it — nothing to cut at, nothing to frighten, nobody to talk to. It was told to keep people out of a room and it is still doing that.
notes: It has no eyes. What it has instead is an awareness of movement in the space immediately around it, and beyond that radius it genuinely cannot find anybody.
provenanceNotes: A suit of plate standing 6 feet, which is the SM 0 row.

HP is bought above ST because an object's durability is a property of its mass and construction, not of how hard it can push. FP is stated rather than derived: a thing with no metabolism would otherwise be rated as if it tired.

monsters.name: Awakened Shrub
monsters.lair: Wherever it was rooted when the spell found it, and a slow shuffling radius around that.

attacks.name: Rake
attacks.notes: Thorns dragged across whatever is in reach. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A waist-high bush that has been given a mind and, unluckily for it, a clear understanding of its position. It talks, it remembers who planted it, and it cannot defend itself against anybody with an axe. Most awakened shrubs end up as somebody's informant.
notes: An awakened plant is awake in the full sense and will hold a conversation, which is generally why it is in the scene at all.
Fire is the obvious answer to it. There is no vulnerability on the stat block, so a GM should rule that at the table.
provenanceNotes: About three feet across, which is the SM -2 row.

monsters.name: Awakened Tree
monsters.lair: The stand of wood it grew in, which it now considers its responsibility.

attacks.name: Branch
attacks.notes: A limb the thickness of a man's waist, swung on a slow arc that is very hard to be somewhere else for.

monsters.description: Twenty feet of oak with opinions. An awakened tree walks at a pace it can hold for days and hits like a falling beam. It is usually not hostile, but it has watched its wood for a long time and it knows precisely who has been cutting.
provenanceNotes: About twenty feet, which is the SM +3 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it lifts and moves timber, which is the heaviest thing it does.
DX 6 is the point of the creature. It hits enormously hard and is trivially easy to avoid, and a party that stands still is making a choice.

monsters.name: Clay Golem
monsters.lair: The vault, tomb or laboratory it was fired in and has not left since.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: A fist of fired clay the size of a helmet. It does not wind up and it does not stop.

monsters.description: Eight feet of fired clay in a rough human shape, standing in front of whatever it was made to guard. It is slow, it is not clever, and very little a blade does to it matters. Damage makes it worse rather than better: past a point it stops guarding and starts attacking, and there is no calling it off after that.
provenanceNotes: Eight feet, which is the SM +1 row.
Unliving rather than Homogenous: a golem is at least built like a body, with limbs that can be broken off, which a rug or a sword is not.
Berserk is the creature's defining behavior and is bought as the published disadvantage rather than written only into the prose.

monsters.name: Flying Sword
monsters.lair: A rack, a stone hand, or the middle of the air above a doorway.

attacks.name: Blade
attacks.notes: A longsword swung by nothing. The damage is the blade's, not any muscle behind it.

monsters.description: A sword hanging point-down at chest height, turning slowly to face whoever came in. It fences well, and there is no body behind it to threaten and no face to read. Breaking the blade is the only reliable way to stop it.
provenanceNotes: A longsword is about 3 ft 6 in, which is the SM -1 row.

Damage is stated as literal dice rather than derived from ST: the injury comes from the edge and the enchantment, not from a Strength that does not exist. The builder takes literal dice only where a spec states them.
Flight is bought at full price with no Winged limitation — the thing simply hangs in the air, and nothing about it can be grounded by clipping a wing.

monsters.name: Rug of Smothering
monsters.lair: A floor, indistinguishable from every other rug in the building until somebody stands on it.

attacks.name: Smother
attacks.notes: It comes up off the floor and wraps. No damage at all: the victim is blinded, held, and suffocating, and everyone else in the room has to decide whether they can cut a rug without cutting the person inside it.

monsters.description: It is a rug. It stays a rug until it is over somebody's head, at which point it weighs as much as a man and has folded itself twice. It does no damage at all. The victim suffocates inside it while everyone else works out how to help without putting a blade through them.
provenanceNotes: Ten feet on the long side, which is the SM +1 row.

It has no damaging attack at all, and the whole record rests on binding ST and a suffocation ability. That is the correct shape and it is also a good check on the rating path, which would score a creature that deals no damage at zero if the disabling ability were not priced.
Stealth is bought high on purpose. Its entire advantage is being furniture until it is not.
